title: Finite residue fields and evaluation at Tate maximal ideals
statement:
For a complete field $F$ with a nontrivial real-valued nonarchimedean absolute value and $r\geq0$, write $T_r(F)=F\langle x_1,\ldots,x_rangle$ for the ring of series $\sum_{
u\in\mathbf N^r}c_
u x^
u$ such that for every $\epsilon>0$ only finitely many $|c_
u|\geq\epsilon$, with coefficientwise addition and Cauchy multiplication. Let $\mathfrak n$ be a maximal proper ideal of $T_r(F)$, and put $L=T_r(F)/\mathfrak n$. Then $L$ has finite degree over $F$, meaning it is a finite $F$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. It carries a unique real-valued nonarchimedean absolute value extending that of $F$, and is complete for it. Put $a_i=x_i mod\mathfrak n\in L$; then $|a_i|\leq1$. For every $h=\sum_
u c_
u x^
u\in T_r(F)$ the quotient map is given by the convergent sum $$h mod\mathfrak n=\sum_
u c_
u a^
u\in L.$$ This includes $r=0$, when $L=F$ and $\mathfrak n=0$.

source.place: Conrad, Several approaches to non-archimedean geometry, §1.1 preliminary finite-extension paragraph, Exercise 1.1.4, Theorem 1.1.5(1), and the paragraph immediately following it (PDF pp.2–4); read online 2026-10-24, archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: First prove by induction on $r$ that all maximal residue fields are finite over $F$. For $r=0$, $T_0(F)=F$, whose only maximal proper ideal is zero. Suppose $r>0$ and the assertion holds for $r-1$. By [lem-trf-restricted-series-gauss-completion] the Tate rings have their complete Gauss norms and admit regrouping in the last variable. The variable $x_r$ is nonzero and is not a unit: taking the constant coefficient is a ring map to $F$ sending $x_r$ to zero. Hence $T_r(F)$ is not a field. Its maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$ cannot be zero (otherwise its quotient would make this ring a field), so choose $0\ne f\in\mathfrak n$.

source.place: Conrad §1.1, Theorem 1.1.5(1), preliminary finite-extension paragraph and Exercise 1.1.4 (PDF pp.2–4). Agent reconstruction of the omitted induction and boundedness argument; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-tate-triangular-distinguished-coordinate] to $f$. Replace $\mathfrak n$ by $\sigma(\mathfrak n)$; the induced quotient isomorphism fixes $F$, so finiteness for this quotient proves finiteness for the original one. Write $A=T_{r-1}(F)$, $D=A\langle x_r\rangle$ and $g=v\sigma(f)\in\sigma(\mathfrak n)$ with distinguished degree $d$. By [lem-trf-tate-weierstrass-norm-division] the ideal $(g)$ equals $(w)$ for a monic $w\in A[x_r]$ of degree $d$, and division represents every class modulo $(w)$ by a polynomial of degree less than $d$. If $d=0$, $g$ is a unit, contradicting properness of $\sigma(\mathfrak n)$. Thus $d\ge1$, and the images of $1,x_r,\ldots,x_r^{d-1}$ generate the field $L^{\prime}=D/\sigma(\mathfrak n)$ as an $A$-module.

source.place: Conrad §1.1, Theorem 1.1.5(1), preliminary finite-extension paragraph and Exercise 1.1.4 (PDF pp.2–4). Agent reconstruction of the omitted induction and boundedness argument; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Let $B$ be the image of $A$ in $L^{\prime}$. The same generators make $L^{\prime}$ a finite $B$-module, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral] makes every element integral over $B$. For $0\ne b\in B$, apply this to $b^{-1}\in L^{\prime}$: a relation $(b^{-1})^e+c_{e-1}(b^{-1})^{e-1}+\cdots+c_0=0$, $e\ge1$, gives $b^{-1}=-c_{e-1}-c_{e-2}b-\cdots-c_0b^{e-1}\in B$. Thus $B$ is a field and $\ker(A\to L^{\prime})$ is maximal. By the induction hypothesis $B$ has a finite $F$-spanning set $b_1,\ldots,b_t$. Products $b_jx_r^i$, $1\le j\le t$, $0\le i<d$, span $L^{\prime}$ over $F$: expand first over $B$ using step 2, and then each coefficient over $F$. This completes the induction and proves the stated finite-module assertion for $L$.

source.place: Conrad §1.1, Theorem 1.1.5(1), preliminary finite-extension paragraph and Exercise 1.1.4 (PDF pp.2–4). Agent reconstruction of the omitted induction and boundedness argument; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Every element of the finite-dimensional field extension $L/F$ is algebraic: powers $1,z,\ldots,z^e$ are linearly dependent once $e$ is the size of a finite basis. Apply [lem-trf-spectral-norm-algebraic-extension] to equip $L$ with its multiplicative nonarchimedean absolute value extending that of $F$. The compatibility with scalar multiplication in that statement makes $L$ a normed $F$-vector space. By [lem-per-finite-normed-space-complete] it is complete. By [lem-sfb-algebraic-absolute-value-unique] any other extending absolute value agrees with this one. This applies also to inseparable extensions.

source.place: Conrad §1.1, Theorem 1.1.5(1), preliminary finite-extension paragraph and Exercise 1.1.4 (PDF pp.2–4). Agent reconstruction of the omitted induction and boundedness argument; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Let $\pi:T_r(F)\to L$ be the quotient map, now using the original coordinates. The isometric finite extension $F\hookrightarrow L$ satisfies [lem-per-tate-finite-scalar-extension], which identifies $T_r(F)\otimes_F L$ with $T_r(L)$ by $h\otimes\lambda\mapsto\lambda j(h)$, where $j$ applies the inclusion to coefficients. The bilinear map $(h,\lambda)\mapsto\pi(h)\lambda$ induces a map $\mu:T_r(F)\otimes_F L\to L$ by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. On pure tensors it preserves products, since $\pi(hh^{\prime})\lambda\lambda^{\prime}=\pi(h)\lambda\pi(h^{\prime})\lambda^{\prime}$; it preserves $1$ and scalar multiplication as well. Pure tensors generate, so distributivity proves that $\mu$ is a unital $L$-algebra map. Compose with the inverse scalar-extension isomorphism to obtain $\chi:T_r(L)\to L$ with $\chi(j(h))=\pi(h)$. By [lem-trf-restricted-series-gauss-completion], $T_r(L)$ is a complete normed $L$-algebra with $\|1\|=1$. Therefore [lem-per-banach-character-norm-bound] gives $|\pi(h)|\le\|j(h)\|=\|h\|$, the equality following coefficientwise from the isometry $F\hookrightarrow L$. In particular $|a_i|=|\pi(x_i)|\le1$.

proof.text:
For $h=\sum_
u c_
u x^
u$, put $h_N=\sum_{|
u|\le N}c_
u x^
u$. By [lem-trf-restricted-series-gauss-completion], $\|h-h_N\|	o0$. Step 5 gives $|\pi(h)-\pi(h_N)|\le\|h-h_N\|	o0$. For a polynomial, the homomorphism identities give $\pi(h_N)=\sum_{|
u|\le N}c_
u a^
u$. Thus these sums converge to $\pi(h)$. They also define the unordered convergent sum in the statement: since $|a_i|\le1$, $|c_
u a^
u|\le|c_
u|$, so outside any sufficiently large finite exponent set every finite tail has norm less than a prescribed $\epsilon>0$ by the strong triangle inequality. Completeness of $L$ gives convergence, and the degree truncations have that same limit. For $r=0$ there is one exponent, the empty tuple; the sum is the constant coefficient and the quotient is $F/0=F$.

lean.statement: theorem tate_maximal_residue_evaluation (F : Type u) [NormedField F] [IsUltrametricDist F] [CompleteSpace F] (hF : ∃ c : F, c ≠ 0 ∧ ‖c‖ ≠ 1) (r : ℕ) (n : Ideal ↥(MvPowerSeries.IsRestricted.subring (R := F) (fun _ : Fin r ↦ (1 : ℝ)))) [n.IsMaximal] : @Module.Finite F _ _ _ (tateResidueScalar F r n).toAlgebra.toModule ∧ (∃ v : AbsoluteValue (↥(MvPowerSeries.IsRestricted.subring (R := F) (fun _ : Fin r ↦ (1 : ℝ))) ⧸ n) ℝ, (∀ c : F, v (tateResidueScalar F r n c) = ‖c‖) ∧ IsNonarchimedean v ∧ @CompleteSpace _ v.toNormedRing.toUniformSpace ∧ (∀ w : AbsoluteValue (↥(MvPowerSeries.IsRestricted.subring (R := F) (fun _ : Fin r ↦ (1 : ℝ))) ⧸ n) ℝ, (∀ c : F, w (tateResidueScalar F r n c) = ‖c‖) → w = v) ∧ (∀ i : Fin r, v (tateResidueCoordinate F r n i) ≤ 1) ∧ (∀ h : ↥(MvPowerSeries.IsRestricted.subring (R := F) (fun _ : Fin r ↦ (1 : ℝ))), @HasSum _ (Fin r →₀ ℕ) _ v.toNormedRing.toUniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace (fun ν ↦ tateResidueScalar F r n (MvPowerSeries.coeff ν h.val) * ν.prod (fun i e ↦ tateResidueCoordinate F r n i ^ e)) (Ideal.Quotient.mk n h) (SummationFilter.unconditional (Fin r →₀ ℕ)))) ∧ (r = 0 → n = ⊥ ∧ Function.Bijective (tateResidueScalar F r n))
